title: oncall-signal-poisoning-investigation-notes
content:
Summary:

This note documents an on-call investigation into a sustained flurry of high-severity pagers over a 6-hour window that ultimately traced to 'signal poisoning' of a core telemetry pipeline. The incident surfaced as inflated 95th/99th latency SLO burn entries and synthetic-check failures that were not reflected in user-reported errors.

Impact:
- Intermittent SLO burn incidents for inference-hosted-api:api-gateway (5xx rate spike alerts firing every ~30m).
- Pager noise: multiple oncall rotations paged for the same symptom; reduced availability of engineers for genuine downstream incidents.
- Root-cause customer impact: none confirmed; discrepancy between synthetic metrics and customer support tickets.

Detection and initial triage (timeline):
- 2026-02-18 01:12 UTC — First pager: "SLO: inference-hosted-api 99p latency > 1200ms (5m)". Pager routed to core-platform oncall.
- 01:20 UTC — Multiple similar pagers across regions; synthetics for eu-west and us-west show spike in tail latency.
- 01:34 UTC — Oncall run preliminary checklist: verify infra health, pods, autoscaler metrics, GPU utilization. All nominal.
- 01:46 UTC — Observability team joins; traced alerts to aggregator job that computes percentile distributions for latency SLO.
- 02:02 UTC — Investigation hypothesis: a recent metrics transformation PR changed timestamp handling and introduced duplication of some latency samples in the distribution aggregation.
- 02:15 UTC — Temporary mitigation: mute aggregation-derived SLO alerting rules and enable a fallback SLO computed from direct listener histograms.
- 03:05 UTC — Root cause identified: a downstream shim (metrics-enricher v2.8.1) started replaying a small subset of recently ingested spans with future timestamps when the ingestion queue hit backpressure. This created duplicated samples that disproportionately impacted percentiles.
- 03:45 UTC — Hotfix: rollback metrics-enricher to v2.8.0 in all regions. Aggregator dedup heuristics adjusted (short-term).
- 04:30 UTC — Alerts stabilized; no new false SLO burns after rollback.

Evidence collected:
- Aggregator logs show ~3% of records had ns-level timestamp shifts (+600s) and duplicate trace_ids.
- Histogram from raw listener shows smooth latency distribution; aggregated percentile diverged only after enrichment.
- Grafana dashboards annotated with correlating deploy events around 2026-02-18 00:55 UTC.
- Synthetic pings to the inference API showed consistent tail latency before and after incident; customers did not open matching error tickets.

Root cause analysis (hypothesis -> confirmation):
- Hypothesis 1: Upstream load caused backpressure and the enricher retried messages with a bug that advanced timestamps. Confirmed by logs and reproducer run locally with backpressure scenario.
- Hypothesis 2: Aggregator dedupe logic assumed idempotent trace_id+timestamp pairs; the timestamp advance broke dedupe. Confirmed when dedupe bypassed on modified timestamps.
- Contributing factor: No synthetic or alerting rule validated aggregator outputs against raw histograms; alerting solely relied on aggregator percentiles.

Mitigation and immediate fixes performed:
- Rolled back metrics-enricher to last known-good v2.8.0 in all kube clusters.
- Temporarily suppressed aggregator-based SLO alerts and switched to listener-derived SLOs for 72 hours of monitoring.
- Added short-term aggregator-side dedupe that normalizes timestamps within a 1s window for identical trace_ids.

Longer-term corrective actions and runbook updates:
- (Owner: Chen Wei) Implement a canary validation step for any pipeline component that mutates telemetry: new deploys must run a 1-hour async validation comparing aggregator percentiles vs raw histograms on a sample stream before promoting. ETA: 2026-03-05.
- (Owner: Amara Singh) Update SLO alerting policy to require two independent signals (aggregator AND raw-listener) before a page at severity P1. Add a "discordant-signal" label for pages triggered by only one source. ETA: 2026-03-01.
- (Owner: Priya Raman) Add unit/integration tests in metrics-enricher to ensure no timestamp advancement on retries and add a property-based test for idempotence. ETA: 2026-03-08.
- (Owner: Miguel Alvarez) Create a lightweight reconciliation job that runs every 10 minutes to compare aggregator percentiles with raw histograms and emit an anomaly metric when divergence > 5%. ETA: 2026-03-12.
- Documented a stop-gap runbook section: "If SLO shows burn but customer-impact telemetry (errors, support tickets, API error rates) is low, verify aggregator vs raw-listener divergence before paging the infra pager." (added to oncall-runbook v2).

Runbook snippets (to be integrated into canonical runbook):
1) On receiving latency SLO page:
   a) Check raw-listener histogram panel for same time window.
   b) Check aggregator logs for recent deploys and enrichment component versions.
   c) If histogram and aggregator disagree by >5% on 99p, escalate to Observability team and mute aggregator-derived pages for that SLO; switch to raw-listener-derived alerting.
   d) If both signals agree, follow standard latency mitigation (check JVM GC, NVidia GPU stalls, autoscaler).

2) For metrics pipeline deploys:
   a) Run sample-stream validation (local simulation of backpressure).
   b) Verify dedupe invariants for trace_id+timestamp idempotence.
   c) Post-deploy, check reconciliation job anomalies for 1 hour.

Lessons learned and wider recommendations:
- Single-source-of-truth anti-pattern: relying on a transformed aggregation as sole truth for pages increases blast radius when transformer bugs appear. We should prefer cross-checking transformed signals with raw-weighted signals.
- Alert ergonomics: pages triggered by a single pipeline should be labeled differently ("pipeline-sourced") and routed to Observability first rather than platform infra. This reduces context-switching and faster diagnosis.
- Backpressure testing gap: production-ish backpressure scenarios were not in the CI matrix for metrics-enricher. Add heavy-tail and retry behavior tests.

Follow-ups and open todos:
- [ ] Create INF-2345: Add canary validation pipeline (owner Chen).
- [ ] Create INF-2346: Adjust oncall escalation routing for pipeline-sourced pages (owner Priya).
- [ ] Add chaos experiment to simulate backpressure and ensure enricher retry correctness (owner Miguel).
- [ ] Update oncall-runbook v2 and schedule a 30-min walkthrough in SRE weekly (owner Amara).

Appendix: quick debugging checklist (copy-able):
- Are customer-facing metrics (5xx, user latency from RUM or logs, support tickets) elevated? If no -> suspect pipeline/transformer.
- Inspect aggregator->enricher logs for message replay patterns and timestamp deltas.
- Compare aggregator percentile vs listener histogram for same time bucket.
- If dedupe logic exists, find last deploy touching dedupe or timestamp handling.

Notes to self (rough):
- Consider adding a label on metrics ("pipeline_version") so alerts can automatically include the pipeline binary version. Will help triage.
- Might be worth a lightweight "alert sanity" job that checks for anomalous increases in percentile variance vs mean every 10 minutes and suppresses until human review. But be careful not to hide real incidents.

End of notes.

-- Priya R., oncall SRE
